items.title: Representation of Hindustan Pesticides Manufacturer Association (HPMA) for request to impose ban on import of agro-chemicals that Indian Industry is capable of producing- to support “Make in India” boost domestic manufacturing and reduce trade dependence. The agenda was deliberated in details on all aspects of the representation. During the elaborated discussion it was submitted by the Experts that the 9(3) original registrations are granted for the registration of an insecticide, after such enquiry as it deems fit and after satisfying itself that the insecticide to which the application relates conforms to the claims made by the importer or by the manufacturer, as the case may be, as regards the efficacy of the insecticide and its safety to human beings and animals. It was further noted that the IA, 1968 states that the 9(4) registrations can be granted on the basis of 9(3). The provision reads as under: Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 “Notwithstanding anything contained in the section where an insecticide has been registered on the application of any person, any other person desiring to import or manufacture the insecticide or engaged in the business of import or manufacture thereof, shall, on application and on payment of prescribed fee be allotted a registration number and granted a certificate of registration in respect thereof on the same conditions on which the insecticide was originally- registered.” The above provision infers that all the Registration of Product/Molecule has to be given a unique registration number and separate Registration Certificate has to be generated for each Molecule or Product to each applicant which shall be a mirror image of original registrant U/s 9(3) in terms of Chemical Composition etc. It was also informed that as per available information on the website more than 660 source of import are registered in India by the RC for Import of different molecules/products to be used in the country and very few applicants has submitted the complete details of source of import including the manufacturing address of the overseas country. After detailed evaluation of information and provisions the
items.decision: RC decided as under: 1. The Manufacturing address as well as office address of all the registered import sources of all the registered product/molecules registered for use in the country should be obtained from the stake holders with Geo Tagging details in the form of documentary evidence such as manufacturing license etc issued by the regulatory authorities of Source country/overseas country. The documents should be Government approved only. 2. The new applicants shall mandatorily submit the above required information with their applications. 3. The above said requirement shall also be treated as a part and parcel of the relevant applicable guidelines and shall also be included into the requirement in the guidelines. 4. 9(4) TI endorsement of additional Source shall not be allowed, if the Chemical Composition of already granted CR is different from the source sought to be endorsed. In such cases applicant has to obtained fresh CR as per guidelines U/s 9(4) TI category to enhance the transparency in case of quality control and collation of data. 5. 9(4) TI endorsement cases of extension of validity, Change of address, Purity of the product etc of such source shall not be permitted whose CC is different from 9(3) registrant and/or does not match with the 9(3) original registrant. (One Chemical Composition One CR is the principal rationale). The RC further directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to issue a public notice for appropriate compliance by all Stakeholders, copies of the same also be communicated to all Pesticides Associations for creating awareness to their member companies.

items.title: Follow up action on agenda item no. 10.71 of 468th RC meeting w.r.t. the order dated 05.01.2026 passed by the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) in contempt petition (MD) No. 2710/2025 in WP (MD) No. 7813 of 2024 and presently the final order dated 09.01.2026. RC in terms of the observations made by the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) in its order dated 05.01.2026 had withdrawn its final decision taken in its 467th meeting at agenda item no. 2.2.
items.decision: RC perused the final judgement dated 09.01.2026 passed by the Hon’ble High Court and noted the same for compliance. Whereas Hon’ble High Court had directed the RC to take a fresh decision in the matter within a period of 4 weeks. RC shall accordingly draw the proceedings afresh in terms of the Hon’ble Appellate Authority order dated 21.03.2022 and the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) order dated 27.03.2024. Factual Background: Initially M/s Shobika was granted a provisional registration u/s 9(3b) of the Insecticides Act, 1968 at a concentration of 0.55% in the year 2015. Subsequent extensions were also granted for the same and the applicant had commercially used the product for several years. The applicant had applied for 9(3) registration for indigenous manufacture of Alphacypermethrin 0.58% in the year 2020. After due scrutiny of the application and after satisfying itself the RC approved the said application for a concentration of 0.55% in its 435th Meeting. Being dissatisfied with the 0.55% approval, the applicant approached the Hon’ble Appellate Authority by filing an appeal u/s 10 of the Insecticides Act, 1968. The following reasoning was given by the RC to grant registration at 0.55% instead of 0.58% in its impugned decision: 1. Appellant had previously applied for registration u/s 9(3B) of the Act for its LLIN containing 0.55% alphacypermethrin w/w as the active ingredient, which was granted along with commercialization. 2. There is no adverse report from the National Vector Borne Disease Control programme (NVBDCP) qua the LLINs with 0.55% active ingredient. 3. RC cannot consider registration for two products which have the same purpose but have different concentrations of the active ingredient. 4. RC follows the BIS specification wherein formulation compounds are given +10% and -5% of leverage which are under 9% of the active ingredients, where the Appellant had quoted + 25% of leverage, which may affect the quality of LLIN, which cannot be Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 permitted by the RC because, if permitted the appellant then “may have the right to manufacture LLINs at + 25% of the claimed items which have not been tested in Indian circumstances during generating the data to reveal their bio-effectiveness. The Hon’ble Appellate Authority after hearing M/s Shobika and the RC, had made certain observations and had set aside the decision of the RC taken on its 435th meeting at agenda item no. 11.2 wherein the RC had granted the registration on a concentration of 0.55%. Further, RC was directed to consider the application as per Form-I and technical information available on records. In terms of the above order although RC dealt the matter in its various meetings which are the part of record. In the mean while the applicant approached the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) by filing a writ petition no. 7813 of 2024 seeking directions to decide their captioned application of 0.58% in terms of the Appellate Authority Order. The Hon’ble High Court was pleased to pass an order dated 27.03.2024 directing the RC to consider and decide the application of the applicant for 0.58% in terms of the Appellate Authority Order. RC in its wisdom and in view of the fact that the substance sought to be registered is to be used in public health programmes and therefore, RC in order to scientifically deal with the matter had obtained comments from other related authorities including ICMR. Since, the RC was continuously deliberating the matter in its various meeting and hence could not take a final decision within the directed time lines. M/s Shobika had preferred a Contempt Petition before the Hon’ble High Court of Madras alleging willful non compliance of the Appellate Authority order dated 21.03.2022 and the Hon’ble High Court order dated 27.03.2024. During the pendency of the contempt petition the RC had taken a final decision in its 467th meeting at agenda item no. 2.2 whereby the RC has rejected the application of the applicant as the same does not qualify at 0.58% for the reasons mentioned in its final decision. The decision was in harmony of the Expert Committee Report from ICMR also. The Hon’ble High Court after adjudicating the matter had inter-alia found that the RC has committed a contempt by traveling outside the scope of the Appellate Authority Order and the order dated 27.03.2024 passed by the Hon’ble High Court. Now after going through the final order dated 09.01.2026 passed by the Hon’ble High Court and in terms of the observations made by the Appellate Authority in its order dated 21.03.2022 RC observes that although the RC had contested the matter on the grounds mentioned herein below:- 1. No new data was submitted along with Appellant application for registration under section 9(3) of the Act for LLIN containing 0.58% Alphacypermethrin w/w as the active ingredient. 2. The Appellant has not submitted toxicology data on “irritation to mucus membrane (rabbit)” for LLIN having Alphacypermethrin content of 0.58% w/w but has instead submitted the same for LLIN having alphacypermethrin content of 0.57% w/w. 3. Appellant has only generated Phase-III study data on LLIN containing Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 Alphacypermethrin concentration at 0.58% w/w and Phase-1/Phase-II trial/evaluation were not be submitted for Appellant’s LLIN containing Alphacypermethrin concentration at 0.58% w/w. 4. The Appellant had earlier been given provisional registration u/s 9(3B) of the Act for the concentration of 0.55% w/w along with extensions during data generation which the registrant commercially used for about five years and during this period the petitioner had generated only Phase III study data on 0.58% w/w. Scientifically, to rely upon the phase-III study data on 0.58% w/w the petitioner ought to and should have also carried out the data generation for Phase-I and Phase-II at the concentration of 0.58% w/w. 5. That Phase-I and Phase-II studies were carried out at the concentration of 0.55% of alphacypermethrin and accordingly, the provisional certificate u/s 9(3B) with commercialization was granted. However, while applying for grant of registration u/s 9(3) Appellant claimed concentration of Alphacypermethrin at 0.58% which was claimed to be actually used only during Phase-III trial. M/s Shobika had also made the submission before the Appellate Authority as set out herein under :- a. The RC’s opposition to the grant of registration on the ground that the Appellant has not submitted toxicology data on “irritation to mucus membrane (Rabbit)” for LLIN having Alphacypermethrin content 0.58% w/w but has instead submitted the same for LLIN having Alphacypermethrin content of 0.57% w/w, is wholly misconceived and is contrary to its own agenda on toxicity produced by it. To this effect the appellant has relied on the following submission: i. Alphacypermethrin content of 0.57% w/w is well within the tolerance limit of ±25% that is appellant to this product. ii. Even the RC’s expert, in the above agenda on Toxicity did not point out hence, this is not a deficiency. On the contrary it was noted that the product was non irritant and the toxicity expert concluded after examining all toxicity data as under: “Appellant has submitted the data and information on the LLIN as per the laid down conventions guidelines, the case can be presented before the RC with complete fact for deliberation and appropriate decision”; b. Appellant further contends that he has already submitted three years, three locations bio-efficacy trial that were duly conduced in accordance with the protocol of Indian Council for Medical Research (ICMR). c. Further, RC is aware that as per ICMR protocol, Phase-I trial is not required in case the product has been approved by the WHO. RC is also aware that the Appellants product has already been approved by the WHO. d. Appellant has already conduct Phase-II trail prior to Phase -III trial for the product DuraNet with targeted dose containing 0.58% of Alphacypermethrin and the same was submitted during application made u/s 9(3B) of Insecticide Act, 1968. The National Institute of Malaria Research (NIMR), which has been established under the Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 aegis of the ICMR, has conducted the above mentioned Phase-II trail/evaluation for the product DuraNet (which was then owned by Clark Mosquito Control and has subsequently been purchased by the appellant) which target dose containing 0.58% w/w of alphacypermethrin ± 25%. Additionally, Vector Control Research Centre, Pondicherry (VCRC) has also conducted Phase-II trials/evaluation for the Appellant’s LLIN having Alphacypermethrin content of 0.58% w/w. e. Furthermore, RC never raised any query or demand for either Phase-I of Phase-II trials, nor did it raised any deficiency on the ground that Phase-I and Phase-II trials were not submitted for Appellant’s LLIN containing Alphacypermethrin concentration at 0.58% w/w. All this goes to shows that the RC’s suggestion at this stage that Appellant ought to have produced Phase-I and Phase-III trial, is misguided. The observations of the Hon’ble Appellate Authority have been recorded in para 8 of the order dated 21.03.2022and are as under: - It is a given fact that the Appellant product is based on the concentration which has applied for grant of registration u/s 9(3) and the RC ought to have considered the bio- efficacy and toxicity data related to this concentration, which was not done. This only goes to show that the RC’s decision in its 435th meeting vide agenda item no. 11.2 was indeed predetermined and not based on existing protocols and scientific justification. While taking the impugned decision in its 435th meeting for allowing registration of Alphacypermethrin 0.55%, The RC has not expressed any dissatisfaction with the data generated and submitted by the applicant using LLIN containing 0.58% Alphacypermethrin. In fact, that in the past RC has registered the different products for LLIN with Alphacypermethrin as active ingredient as different concentrations. Therefore, I agree that the only aspect the RC should have considered was safety and efficacy of the product at the concentration at which the present application u/s 9(3) of the Act has been made. The appellants submission on meeting all the protocols for generation of Phase-I, II and III trial data is based on clear scientific justification and existing protocols. Further as it revealed from the contents of impugned decision that RC never raised any query or demand asking for either Phase-I or Phase-II trails evaluations nor did it raised any deficiency on the ground that Phase-I and Phase-II trial evaluati9on were not submitted for the Appellant LLIN containing Alphacypermethrin concentration at 0.58% w/w. Therefore, RC’s observation in its written submission that the appellant ought to have produce Phase-I and Phase-II trail evaluation is an after thought. Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 It is fact that the LLINs are used worldwide and there is not scientific material relied upon by RC to suggest that mosquitoes has developed resistance to LLINs with Alphacypermethrin at 0.58% concentration. In fact own close perusal of the large scale bioefficacy trials conducted by National Central for Diseases Control (NCDC) on appellants product it is clear that the results are to the contrary. This appellate Authority gave CIB&RC ample scope to produce relevant scientific evidence on this aspects which CIB&RC could not be produce. Based on the contentions raised by the applicant and the CIB&RC; the Appellate Authority had recorded the above observations and accordingly the decision of the RC taken in its 435th meeting at agenda item no. 11.2 was set-aside and the directions were given to the RC to consider the grant of registration of the captioned application on 0.58% based on technical information available on record within a period of one month. Analysis: RC also observes that the submissions and contentions made by the RC before the Hon’ble Appellate Authority were not accepted and accordingly the decision of the 435th meeting was set-aside. RC also observes that the Hon’ble High Court of Madras (Madurai Bench) vide its order dated 05.01.2026 had clearly observed that the RC although had dealt the matter in its various meetings and had taken a final decision in 467th meeting traveling outside of the scope of the directions given by the Appellate Authority and has attempted to re-open the issues which were already adjudicated by the Appellate Authority. The Hon’ble High Court, in view of the fact that the decision of the RC taken in its 467th meeting stands withdrawn, has further been pleased to grant four weeks to pass a fresh order in terms of the directions given by the Appellate Authority and the Hon’ble High Court vide its order dated 27.03.2024. The RC perused the technical records pertaining to the matter and without entering into any further examination or analysis and in terms of the observations made by the Appellate Authority, notes that the tolerance limit of ± 25% although not applicable to the present matter but since the same is viewed by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority, the subject application of the applicant for 0.58% is again considered. RC also noted that since the matter has been adjudicated by the Hon’ble Appellate Authority and the Hon’ble High Court therefore, no further re-examination of the matter is needed. Accordingly, RC decided to grant the approval for LLIN containing Alphacypermethrin 0.58% w/w for indigenous manufacture to M/s Shobika. Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 RC makes it clear that this decision has been taken in the peculiar set of circumstances as enumerated above and shall not be construed as the precedent for any future purposes in any reference or case.

items.title: To explore provision for auto approval of preliminary scrutiny and cancellation or closure of applications for non-submission of requisite information within the stipulated time frame.
items.decision: RC deliberated the agenda in detail and decided as under: 1. As per the existing procedure, all the applications are passed through the preliminary scrutiny within a time limit of 5 days as on date. In this regard, the RC decided that the time limit of preliminary scrutiny may be extended to 7 days. Further, RC directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to ask the CGG to enhance the time limit upto 7 days in place of 5 days for preliminary scrutiny. 2. It shall be the responsibility of the concerned expert, if the file is not verified within 7 days or non-submission of data by the applicant as per applicable guidelines, excluding the genuine request for waiving off data. 3. It shall also be ensured that no file is accepted with lack of data whatsoever it may be, such as under generation of data for Shelf-Life OR bio-efficacy or any other data. 4. If, the file has been considered by the Experts during preliminary scrutiny, No deficiency shall be raised for lack of data and concerned Expert shall be solely responsible for this lapse. 5. The CGG may be asked to enable a provision for automated reminders/alerts to be generated through the CROP Portal on the 5th, 6th and 7thday to the concerned expert to ensure timely completion of preliminary scrutiny. It was also approved that the auto- approved files should also be flagged in the Secretary (CIB&RC) account for information and cognizance. 6. No file shall be moved to Park category, henceforth, if applicant is not submitting the deficiency reply in consonance of time line approved by RC in its 400th RC meeting vide agenda item No. 3.3. Such files will be closed automatically in CROP Portal and CGG has to make a provision for automatic closure of such applications. 7. All the applications under Parked category will be considered closed due to non- submission of response by the applicant as per 400th RC meeting decision of time line. The details of such files which stands approved as closed are attached as Annexure- 10.25.1. 8. Further, the RC directed the Sectt. of CIB&RC to issue a public Notice and ask the applicant to submit a requisition with relevant details to the RC within 30 days for revival of their application, if any. 9. If, any file is approved for opening or revival by the RC, after due consideration, in such scenario the applicant has to apply afresh and new file no. has to be generated by Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 the CROP. The scrutiny comments of the concerned Expert of such old closed/revived file may be taken into account. 10. It was also decided that the existing CROP Portal dashboard should have a feature for monitoring expert-wise performance for a desired period. Accordingly, the CGG team is directed to develop and incorporate suitable features in the Portal to enable monitoring and tracking of the performance of each expert. Such monitoring facility should be enabled in login of Department's Admin account. The RC also emphasized that there should be a section in the portal for tracking of file with complete history in chronological order.

Before consideration of the proposal of M/s FMC India Pvt. Ltd., for grant of registration for import of Tetflupyrolimet technical 91% w/w min. u/s section 9(3). The Registration Committee (RC) deliberated the agenda of M/s FMC India Pvt. Ltd. for registration of Tetflupyrolimet Technical (91% w/w minimum) under Section 9(3).
items.decision: The Committee noted concerns regarding the purity issue, as the applicant has sought registration of Tetflupyrolimet at 97% purity in the country of origin (USA), and the entire dossier has been generated using technical material with purity in the range of 99.1% to 96.06%. It indicates that the dossier has been prepared for a 97% product. BIS does not support such a purity gap (97% vs 91%), and even the EPA has reservations for this purity gap. The proposed 91% technical material represents a lower purity grade compared to the 97% product and may contain a higher proportion of impurities, which may require further refinement to meet higher purity specifications. (ii) implications of the DHODH mode of Minutes of 469th RC meeting held on 10.02.2026 action, on potential human and possible cross-resistance with medically relevant drugs specially antifungal drugs; India is a tropical country where fungal infections are prevalent, especially among agricultural workers due to prevailing conditions in the agricultural fields. (iii) immunotoxicity studies in view of the mechanism of action; and, as DHODH inhibition is linked to immune regulation (iv) PFAS-related concerns, including environmental persistence, degradation (such as TFA and other ultra-short-chain PFAS), and long-term toxicity aspects. After deliberation, the RC decided that the applicant/stakeholder be invited to make a detailed presentation addressing the above issues with supporting scientific data. The matter shall be considered thereafter.
